messages:
roxanne: Quick sync on continuous-batcher followups. want to propose an "adaptive expedited lane" approach and get feedback before i write up the RFC v2.
maria_r: Curious — how is "expedited" different from tiny-fast queue or probabilistic fastpath?
roxanne: Expedited = small, bounded reserved capacity per-GPU that can be temporarily stolen based on urgency signals. unlike tiny-fast it doesn't create a forever separate queue; unlike probabilistic fastpath it's deterministic up to a cap.
akash_k: Sounds promising. main win is predictable tail latency for interactive requests without fully fragmenting packer heuristics. what's the admission surface look like?
roxanne: admission returns queue_tag + slot_token + an urgency hint. workers only honor slot_token warmups if canary enabled. minimal API sketch:
```
POST /v1/admit
{ model: "m-id", token_count: 3, urgency?: "interactive"|"normal", cache_hint?: "warm" }
-> { enqueued: true, slot_token: "s:v1:xyz", queue_tag: "expedited", expected_wait_ms_est: 12 }
```
linh_t: minor: rename `urgency` -> `priority_class` to avoid UX collisions. also need clarity on expected_wait_ms_est semantics (estimate at enqueue time).
roxanne: good call. `priority_class` sounds better. and yes, make it explicit in docs that expected_wait_ms_est is a best-effort estimate.
sam_sre: ops checklist: per-queue circuit-breaker, per-tenant kill-switch, and explicit cost dashboard for expedited usage. if reserved lanes blow cost, we must be able to throttle to 0 immediately.
jess_pm: product ask: make sure defaults are conservative. customers shouldn't opt into warmups by accident and see a bill surprise. document button in console with a confirmation.
akash_k: implementation notes: reserve R microbatches per GPU for expedited lane. admission fills expedited until capacity; if full, either enqueue to main packer or fall back to probabilistic fastpath if circuit allows. also track headroom credits per-tenant to avoid abuse.
roxanne: on warmups: slot_token is opaque. workers may call KV.Pin(slot_token) to keep KV alive. we must protect against warmup stampedes: per-model dedupe + short TTL dedupe cache (~200ms) and cap concurrent warms per-device.
linh_t: dedupe window should be configurable per-model based on model cold-start cost. also emit metrics warmup_attempts_total, warmup_dedupe_total, warmup_concurrency_gauge.
sam_sre: add alerts: warmup_dedupe_rate > 0.9 over 5m => P1, sustained warmup concurrency > threshold => P1. and fastpath_cost_usd spike alert.
akash_k: preemption question: rather than splitting inflight batches, rely on expedited reserve and DrainHint. if an urgent token arrives and reserve is empty, request DrainHint on oldest non-urgent batch; worker may early-flush if cost of split > benefit. keeps coupling loose.
roxanne: agreed. no hard preempt in v1. instrument drain_hint_requested_total and drain_hint_honored_total.
jess_pm: rollout plan idea: v1 telemetry-only; v2 enable reserve at 1% of GPUs for internal canaries; v3 enable warmups for selected tenants; v4 ramp reserve and fastpath with cost guardrails.
sam_sre: rollout ops: FF per-region/pool, global kill-switch, synthetic tiny-vs-stream job for canaries, and a rollback doc that flips FF off and forces legacy shaper. verify queue drain <5m in rollback check.
linh_t: one more edge: lost slot_token mid-flight. define behavior: worker treats as cold-exec, tags exec_cold=true, increments slot_token_loss_total. target loss <0.1%. document recovery steps.
akash_k: curious about cost model: reserved lanes cost comes from underutilization. propose a burst-tax alternative where small requests consume an urgency credit token to jump. compare both in sim: cost-per-1M tokens vs p99 latency.
roxanne: yes, we should A/B them in the sim harness. ad-hoc plan: build a sim that can vary burstiness, urgent fraction, and arrival autocorrelation. measure p50/p95/p99 and cost-per-1M tokens.
sam_sre: prometheus names to standardize now: admission_enqueues_total{queue_tag,model,tenant}, admission_rejects_total{reason}, admission_expected_wait_seconds_summary, worker_execs_total{model,queue_tag,tenant,exec_cold}, warmup_attempts_total, warmup_dedupe_total, warmup_concurrency_gauge, drain_hint_requested_total, drain_hint_honored_total, queue_circuit_tripped_total, expedited_reserved_utilization_gauge.
jess_pm: include a short user-facing explainer in the console docs: when to use `priority_class: interactive` and cost implications.
akash_k: implementation micro-ops: keep admission shim extremely cheap. put hotpath in Rust and expose shared-memory state for workers to read queue_tag/shim-version without RPC. fallback RPC if shm missing. target shim <1us resident path.
linh_t: also protect against stampede of warmups: warmup queue should be rate-limited and deduped. if warmup backlog grows, circuit-break warmups and rely on cold executions. alert and rollback.
roxanne: decision for now: prototype adaptive expedited lane + warmup dedupe, run sims vs burst-tax, and measure cost/latency tradeoffs. no hard preempt in v1. action items: akash -> prototype shim + reserve logic, linh -> implement warmup dedupe + metrics, sam -> dashboards/alerts + runbook, jess -> product docs & defaults, me -> RFC follow-up with rollout plan + sim results. ops-bot: ff/expedited-lane-proto created in staging.
ops-bot: feature-flag ff/expedited-lane-proto created in staging.
roxanne: thanks all — i'll post the RFC draft later today. :thumbsup:
